subject: Azure private offer — accelerator credits & channel passback question
messages:
From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@harboredge.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Jules Tan <jules.tan@harboredge.com>
Date: 2028-09-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Azure private offer - accelerator credits + passback question

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier — HarborEdge is interested in buying Redwood via an Azure private offer. Two questions that came up in our procurement sync: 1) We expect some Azure "accelerator" credits from a cloud program that can be applied to Marketplace purchases. Can Redwood accept those credits as part of the private offer settlement, or do they have to flow to your reseller? 2) Our partner (CloudPoint Resellers) requires a minimum channel margin floor (they asked for 15%) — can you document whether the passback to the reseller is gross or net of tax/escrow?

High level numbers: planned first-year commit $750k (US). If helpful, we can share a spreadsheet with the expected accelerator amount and timing. We also need a short statement about invoice routing for compliance.

Could we set up a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through?

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Cloud Procurement
HarborEdge

Attachment: (none in this first mail)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@harboredge.com>, Jules Tan <jules.tan@harboredge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-01T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Azure private offer - accelerator credits + passback question

Alex — thanks for the details. Put Ben (partner sales) and Laura (partner ops) on this thread; Steph for billing nuance. Two quick answers and two asks:

- Short answer on credits: typically accelerator credits are applied on the cloud vendor side; Marketplace settlements depend on the offer wiring. We can accept credits in two models: (A) customer applies credits and pays net to Redwood, or (B) credits flow to reseller/partner and we do a matching credit in our invoicing. We need to confirm the exact Azure program name and credit timing.
- Channel margin: we can model passback as either gross or net, but it changes bookkeeping. Laura — can you check operational constraints for a 15% floor?

Asks:
1) Alex — can you share the accelerator schedule (months and $) and whether Azure requires the credits to be remitted to named resellers?
2) Ben/Laura — I attached an internal margin workback template I want you to fill out with two scenarios (credits flowing to customer vs credits to reseller).
3) Procurement: we should confirm if HarborEdge needs a DocuSignable attestation about invoice routing. If so, we can prepare a short clause.

Proposed: 30-min call 9/2 at 11:00 PT. Works?

Best,
Hannah
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Attachment: margin_workback.xlsx (internal template)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@harboredge.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-01T13:47:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Azure private offer - accelerator credits + passback question

Hannah / team — I filled the margin workback with two scenarios and attached a quick PDF summary. Key points from ops side:

- Scenario A (credits to customer): HarborEdge applies Azure credits against Marketplace line items. Redwood invoices list price; credits reduce net payment to HarborEdge via Azure reconciliation. Result: reseller margin is calculated on list price unless we explicitly net credits before calculating passback.

- Scenario B (credits to reseller): Azure routes credits to CloudPoint. We treat credits as an off-platform rebate to the reseller; passback can be calculated on net after rebate if CloudPoint requests. This requires an explicit passback clause and additional reporting in the private-offer settlement.

Operational caveats: tax treatment varies by jurisdiction; our finance team prefers to calculate reseller passback on net-of-irrecoverable-taxes to avoid downstream disputes. If HarborEdge expects an upfront 15% "floor" on margin, that is doable but will reduce space for accelerator credit absorption — we need to bake it into the waterfall.

I've attached margin_workback.xlsx and a short summary PDF: redwood-private-offer-draft.pdf (pages: model + sample clause). Laura — can you confirm whether our connector to Azure Marketplace supports channel-level credit routing for CloudPoint? If not, we probably need a manual reconciliation cadence (monthly).

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: margin_workback.xlsx, redwood-private-offer-draft.pdf
From: Jules Tan <jules.tan@harboredge.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@harboredge.com>, procurement@harboredge.com
Date: 2028-09-02T07:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Azure private offer - accelerator credits + passback question

Ben / Hannah — thanks for the quick turnaround and the workback. A few clarifications from our procurement/legal:

- HarborEdge's accelerator is a time-bound pool (total $80k spread across months 3-6). Azure requires the credits be applied to the Marketplace buyer account; they cannot be directly routed to a third-party without an explicit reseller billing arrangement.
- CloudPoint is asking for a 15% margin floor on net revenue after all rebates and credits. Their SOW has a clause that if margin falls below 15%, HarborEdge is responsible for a top-up to the reseller.

We attached a signed NDA and the accelerator schedule. We prefer the passback be modeled as: calculate margin on net after Azure credits; if margin < 15% then HarborEdge tops up the difference to CloudPoint. That preserves CloudPoint economics and lets HarborEdge use accelerator credits first.

Quoted for context:
> On Sat, Sep 1, 2028 at 1:47 PM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:
>
> > Operational caveats: tax treatment varies by jurisdiction; our finance team prefers to calculate reseller passback on net-of-irrecoverable-taxes to avoid downstream disputes. If HarborEdge expects an upfront 15% "floor" on margin, that is doable but will reduce space for accelerator credit absorption — we need to bake it into the waterfall.

We'll join the 9/2 11:00 PT call and can have a procurement lead on the line.

Thanks,
Jules
Sr. Procurement Manager | HarborEdge

Subject: Re: Azure private offer - accelerator credits + passback question

Great — thanks for the accelerator schedule and NDA. Quick internal next steps and what we'll bring to the call:

1) Ben/Laura will prepare a final waterfall showing (a) credits-applied-first, (b) reseller margin calc net-of-credits, and (c) a top-up line for HarborEdge per the 15% floor. Expect a one-page appendix with numbers.
2) Finance (Steph) will draft a short attestation clause for the private-offer agreement that documents invoice routing and the top-up obligation.
3) Ops will confirm whether month-end reconciliation or an ongoing Azure connector is the easier route; if connector work is needed, we'll scope effort and include a reconciliation cadence in the MOP.

Call confirmed: 2028-09-02 11:00 PT (calendar invite sent). Please review the attached draft prior to the call — Ben, Laura: finalize the numbers and add the sample clause to the redwood-private-offer-draft.pdf so procurement can review live.

Hannah
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
